clue.text: Essential food the best part of the spread

parts.note: bread is the staple, essential food of the Lord's Prayer's 'daily bread'

indicators.note: the best part of a word is most of it, so the little word 'the' loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Bread, the staple of any meal, is the main element of a laid-out spread of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'best part of' trims 'the' to TH; 'spread' looks like a buffet but means extent or width.
explanation.definitionFit: Spread here is a noun for width or extent, the distance something covers from side to side.

clue.text: Magnanimous about faction in creating division

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the generous word is wrapped around the others

parts.note: magnanimous means generous or big-hearted, i.e. big
a faction is a breakaway group, a sect
taken as written

explanation.surface: A generous leader rises above party factions that are splitting the movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting into two halves is a way of making a division, so the verb form fits 'creating division'.

clue.text: Constant changes alter one, nonetheless

indicators.note: changes tells us the letters of the following words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
read as 'none the less': none is nought, the letter O, and 'the less' says it is subtracted from the pool

explanation.surface: A paradox: the only constant thing is change, yet changes alter everything all the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges ALTER ONE, and 'nonetheless' is read as 'none the less': none is nought, the letter O, which is taken away.
explanation.definitionFit: Constant in the sense of unending or everlasting, never ceasing.

clue.text: Very excited composer, taking in Brazilian city

indicators.note: taking in means one word swallows the other within it

parts.note: Frederick Delius was an English composer
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian city, shortened to Rio

explanation.surface: A composer gets carried away with excitement on a visit to Rio.
explanation.definitionFit: Wildly excited or euphoric, as if in a fevered state.

clue.text: Oxford saint cut with blade, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is pronounced, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: to hew is to cut with an axe or blade

explanation.surface: An Oxford saint was martyred by the sword, or so the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: St Hugh's is an Oxford college named after St Hugh of Lincoln.
explanation.definitionFit: The saint who gave his name to an Oxford college, St Hugh's.

clue.text: He's loaded a doctor's back

parts.note: loaded is slang for wealthy, rich

indicators.note: back means the abbreviation for the doctor is written backwards

explanation.surface: A wealthy man has been helping out a doctor financially.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' is the definition: any man's name can stand for 'he'; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A common man's first name, so it can stand in for a male pronoun.

clue.text: Sea-creature to ridicule with nonsense about silly fin

parts.note: to rib is to tease or ridicule

indicators.note: about means the word for nonsense goes around the jumbled letters

parts.note: bosh is an informal word for nonsense

indicators.note: silly shows the letters of 'fin' are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a sea-creature, talking rubbish about its daft-looking fin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ridicule' as a verb is to tease, and 'silly' scrambles the fin; the creature is a long, flat ribbon-shaped fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, thin, ribbon-shaped marine fish, a kind of sea-creature.

clue.text: Dish that's divided first

indicators.note: first says the word for divided comes at the front

parts.note: divided means cut
that is, i.e.

explanation.surface: A dish of food that has been sliced up before serving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dish' is slang for an attractive person, not a plate of food.
explanation.definitionFit: Dish is slang for a good-looking person, a sweetie.

clue.text: Scholar or student taken in by a Vandyke, possibly

indicators.note: taken in by means the student letter is held inside the following word

parts.note: a Vandyke is a pointed beard, named after the painter van Dyck
L for learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: A scholar or student is deceived by a portrait, possibly one by van Dyck.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Abelard was the twelfth-century French scholar famous for his love of Heloise.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval French philosopher and theologian, a famous scholar.

clue.text: Particularly fine extremes of delicacy

parts.note: the first and last letters of 'delicacy' are ..., and the clue reads them as a pair joined by '&'

explanation.surface: Something especially fine shows delicacy to the utmost degree.
explanation.walkthrough: The outer letters of 'delicacy' are D and Y; say them as 'D & Y' and they become the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dated slang for excellent or splendid, first-rate.

clue.text: Female will remove cases

parts.note: she is the female pronoun
'll is the short form of will

explanation.surface: A woman is going to take the covers off something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Female will' sounds like a woman's intention; it gives SHE + 'LL.
explanation.definitionFit: To shell peas or nuts is to strip off their husks or pods.

clue.text: Novel character as special agent

definitions.meaning: a 1953 novel by L. P. Hartley about a boy carrying secret letters
a person acting as an intermediary between two parties

explanation.surface: A character in a novel works as a secret agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Hartley's novel title, and a word for a messenger or intermediary who negotiates between sides.

clue.text: About to move right in recent grouping of moderates

indicators.note: move right in means a piece of the word 'recent' shifts to its right-hand end

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Recently there has been a regrouping of moderate politicians shifting to the right.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (about) moves from the front of RECENT to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: In politics the middle ground, where parties and voters of moderate views sit.

clue.text: Shrub with flower contrary gardener produced

parts.note: a rose is a flower
the nursery rhyme 'Mary, Mary, quite contrary, how does your garden grow?'

explanation.surface: A shrub and a flower grown by a contrary gardener.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'contrary gardener' is Mary from the English nursery rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: An aromatic evergreen bush used as a herb.

clue.text: City gent's upset about tonight's collapse

indicators.note: about means the reversed word wraps around the jumbled letters
upset in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a gent is a man

indicators.note: collapse shows the letters of 'tonight' fall apart and re-form

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A gentleman is upset that tonight's event has collapsed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' in a down clue turns the gent backwards, and 'collapse' shuffles tonight; the 's on both words is no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An English city in the East Midlands.

clue.text: Snow blocks building

parts.note: read as a weather report, snow is halting construction; read another way, it describes a dwelling made of blocks of snow

explanation.definitionFit: An Inuit dome-shaped shelter built from blocks of packed snow.

clue.text: Cricket side passed over curtly

parts.note: the off side is one half of a cricket field
handed means passed over

explanation.surface: A cricket team was dismissively overlooked for selection.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the off side is the half of the field the batter faces; the answer can serve as an adverb meaning brusquely.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in a brusque, casual manner without courtesy.

clue.text: Considered a century was important

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century
counted means mattered, was important

explanation.surface: Someone reflects that a hundred years was a significant span.
explanation.definitionFit: To be regarded or deemed something, as in being reckoned wise.

clue.text: Orders hay, perhaps, for this

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of the two words could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone orders hay, presumably to feed this animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged words name an animal that eats hay, so the whole clue is also the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy horse that pulls a brewer's cart, and needs hay for feed.

clue.text: Origin of gustatory impairment? It's a tongue condition

indicators.note: origin means the first letter of the following word

parts.note: a loss is an impairment of function
it's expands to it is

explanation.surface: If your sense of taste is impaired, the cause may be a problem with your tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflammation of the tongue, a medical condition affecting it.

clue.text: Salt beef? Consumed about a pound

indicators.note: about places the pound beside the word for consumed, before it

parts.note: beef comes from cattle, an ox
L is the abbreviation for a pound (libra)
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: Salt beef was eaten at about a pound a portion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt beef' is a red herring; 'Salt' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical salt of oxalic acid, found in rhubarb and spinach.

clue.text: Non-belligerent military leader has a drink

parts.note: a conscientious objector, CO, refuses to fight
a commanding officer, CO

explanation.surface: A peaceable army chief has a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot chocolate beverage.

clue.text: Wine Greek character's given to opponent

parts.note: chi is the Greek letter
anti as a noun means an opponent

explanation.surface: Wine served by a Greek to his rival.
explanation.definitionFit: A red wine from Tuscany in Italy.

clue.text: Penchant, might it be, for a final performance?

parts.note: a female swan is a pen, and a song is a chant, so the word splits as pen + chant

explanation.surface: A liking for something might be expressed in one's last show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might it be' signals a reverse clue: the answer, read as a female bird's tune, gives PEN + CHANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A last public appearance or final work, from the legend that swans sing as they die.

clue.text: Brooded about half-boot or other footwear

indicators.note: about means the word for brooded goes around the other piece

parts.note: to brood eggs is to sit on them, so brooded means sat

indicators.note: half here means only the first two of the four letters of 'boot' are used

explanation.surface: Someone brooded over a short boot or some other shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-boot' looks like a type of shoe but means half of 'boot'.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden clog worn in France and the Low Countries.

clue.text: Get off course? Quite!

definitions.meaning: to swerve or deviate from a heading
as an adverb meaning completely, utterly

explanation.definitionFit: To veer away is one sense; the other is the adverb meaning totally or wholly.

clue.text: Punch companion endlessly — wildly hit her

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the puppet's name is cut off

parts.note: Judy is the wife of Punch in the traditional British puppet show

indicators.note: wildly shows the letters of 'hit' are jumbled

explanation.surface: Punch's companion, at the end of her tether, lashes out and hits her.
explanation.walkthrough: Punch and Judy is a British seaside puppet show; 'wildly' turns HIT into ITH.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name, which can stand for the pronoun.

clue.text: Not really one of three sisters, it's clear

definitions.text: Not really one of three sisters
definitions.meaning: the Brontë sisters published under the false surname shared by Currer, Ellis and Acton
clear as a ___, i.e. perfectly clear

explanation.definitionFit: The pen surname of the Brontës, and the ringing object in the simile for clarity.

clue.text: Vehicle to drive off, we bear? This'll help stop it

parts.note: a brake is an old horse-drawn carriage

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word sounds like another

parts.note: to shoo is to drive away, as with birds

explanation.surface: Driving a vehicle off, a passenger asks what will slow it down.
explanation.walkthrough: A brake (or break) is an old open horse-drawn carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: The block that presses against a wheel to slow and halt a vehicle.

clue.text: Often orchestra includes this sort of horn

indicators.note: includes means the letters are found running inside the words

explanation.surface: Orchestras often include a particular horn.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenor horn is a valved brass instrument in E flat.

clue.text: Mathematical formula makes article more complicated

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: complicated shows the letters of 'more' are mixed up

explanation.surface: A mathematical formula makes a piece of writing harder to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposition proved by reasoning, which can be stated as a formula.

clue.text: Protestant worker diluted mixture

indicators.note: mixture shows the letters of 'diluted' are shuffled

explanation.surface: A Protestant labourer has a watered-down drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Protestant' is not the church: it means one who protests, here a worker smashing machinery.
explanation.definitionFit: A nineteenth-century textile worker who protested against machinery by wrecking it.
